text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Algirdas Brazauskas made a test shot from a brand-new anti-tank self propelled machine gun in the Pabrade firing ground, 25 miles nort-east of Vilnius. Lithuania has bought these weapons from Sweden for $5 million.
- Laura Druskinyte, a 16-year-old girl from Varena, 70 miles south of Vilnius, won a $150,000 contract with Paris model agency 'Metropolitan' at a competition last weekend.
- Stepas Visockas, a gypsy candidate to the parliament of Lithuania, was detained on a bus, dogding his fare.
- President Algirdas Brazauskas is disappointed with the parliament's inability to pass a decree to allow the prosecution of two judges who are accused of taking a $2,000 bribe.
- Neris Germanas, a new adviser on international issues to the president, assumes his office today.

- The country's parliament is discussing for the seventh time a draft law on National Radio and Television. If this law is passed the national radio and television company will hold a monopoly and existing independent radio and TV stations would be in jeopardy.
- Construction work in Lithuania dropped by 15.7 percent during the seven months of this year, figures released by the Association of Lithuanian Builders showed.
- Five Western banks are ready to finance the construction of the Butinge oil terminal.
